decisions.choice: the word of the LORD that came to Joel: the heading of the whole book
decisions.reason: The same heading opens Hosea, Micah and Zephaniah. It presents everything that follows, the lament over the locusts, the call to return, the promises and the judgment of the nations, as one message from the LORD given through one man.

decisions.choice: Joel son of Pethuel: the prophet, known only from this book; the book gives no date
alternatives: a date in the ninth century BC, in the reign of King Joash
a date after the exile, in the Persian period
decisions.reason: Nothing is known of Joel or his father Pethuel beyond this verse. The name Joel means "the LORD is God" and was common (1 Samuel 8:2; 1 Chronicles 5:4). Unlike Hosea, Amos or Micah, the heading names no king, and the book never mentions one. It speaks of the temple, its priests and the elders (1:9, 13-14), of Tyre, Sidon and Philistia selling people of Judah to the Greeks (4:4-6), and of Egypt and Edom (4:19). From these hints the book has been dated anywhere from the ninth century BC to after the return from exile, in the fifth or fourth century BC. Its message does not depend on the date.

decisions.choice: The word of the LORD which came to (L); The LORD's word came to (B); This is the message the LORD gave to (R)
decisions.reason: The heading follows the wording set for the Twelve, as in Hosea 1:1. Readable says "message" for "word" and turns the heading into a sentence.

decisions.choice: A palavra do SENHOR que veio a (L); A palavra do SENHOR veio a (B); Esta é a mensagem que o SENHOR deu a (R); Joel, filho de Petuel
alternatives: Palavra do SENHOR, que foi dirigida a
decisions.reason: The heading uses the formula of the prophets' headings in Jeremiah ("A palavra ... que veio a Jeremias"), so the books of the Twelve open alike. The names take their plain Portuguese forms, "Joel" and "Petuel".

decisions.choice: "Palabra del SEÑOR que vino a" (L); "Este mensaje del SEÑOR vino a" (B); "Este es el mensaje que el SEÑOR le dio a" (R); "Joel hijo de Petuel"
decisions.reason: The heading of each of the Twelve follows the Spanish of Jeremiah 1:1-2 at each level; the prophet's name as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: Heading as in Hosea 1:1; "브두엘의 아들 요엘"
decisions.reason: The book-heading formula of the prophets, with the Protestant spellings [Acts 2:16 요엘].

decisions.choice: the heading formula of the Twelve, as Hosea 1:1; the prophet "Joël fils de Petouël"; Joel's oracles are speech, in the present, future and passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: As the term sheet sets for the book headings, the names and the tenses of the Twelve.

decisions.choice: "Lời của CHÚA đã đến với" (L); "Lời CHÚA đến với" (B); "Đây là sứ điệp CHÚA ban cho" (R); "Giô-ên con trai Phê-thu-ên"
decisions.reason: The terms note's heading formula for the Twelve, as in Hosea 1:1, and its form of the names.

decisions.choice: the book-heading formula as Hosea 1:1; "Yoeli mwana wa Pethueli"
decisions.reason: The prophets' heading (term sheet). "Yoeli" as Acts 2:16; "Pethueli" is new and takes the usual final -i.

decisions.choice: Joel as "ኢዩኤል", as Acts 2:16 on main; Pethuel as "ፋቱኤል"
decisions.reason: Peter names the prophet "ኢዩኤል" in the Amharic of Acts 2:16, so the book keeps that form. Pethuel appears only here and is spelled from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: "የእግዚአብሔር ቃል ... መጣ" for "the word of the LORD came", the prophets' formula as in Jeremiah 1:2
decisions.reason: The heading uses the formula set for the prophets (the word of the LORD came to X), so the books of the Twelve open as Jeremiah does. Readable says "መልእክት" (message), as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: the divine name is {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}, inflected inside each option; God's own pronouns take the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: As docs/ukrainian-ot-terms.md sets for every book: the capitals mirror the English "the LORD" and keep the name apart from Adonai; the setting shows the name itself as "Ягве".

decisions.choice: Йоїл, син Петуїла; formulas "говорить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Ягве}}" (L, B) / "каже" (R), "того дня", "день {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}"
decisions.reason: The forms of docs/ukrainian-ot-terms.md, kept the same through the book; "Йоїл" is the form the Ukrainian Acts 2:16 uses.

decisions.choice: योएल, पतूएल
decisions.reason: The prophet keeps the form Acts 2:16 uses for him in this translation (योएल भविष्यद्वक्ता), the same form as the other Joels of Chronicles; his father's name is spelled from the Hebrew Pethuel. Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: का वचन ... के पास पहुँचा (L, B); ने ... यह संदेश दिया (R)
decisions.reason: The prophets note's formula for the word of the LORD coming to a prophet, as the headings of Jeremiah; Readable makes the heading a sentence with संदेश, as the English Readable says "message".

decisions.choice: प्रभु for both YHWH and Adonai; the divine_name setting tells them apart
decisions.reason: Hindi प्रभु translates both the divine name YHWH and the title Adonai ("Lord"). Wherever the Hebrew has the name, प्रभु stands inside a divine_name span whose alternative is याहवे, so a reader who switches the setting sees which is which; where प्रभु stands alone it is Adonai. यहोवा (the Old Version's form) is not used. God takes honorific plural agreement (वे, कहते हैं) in both options.

decisions.choice: Иоиль, сын Пефуила
decisions.reason: Joel keeps the form of Acts 2:16 in this translation (Иоиль). Pethuel is transcribed from the Hebrew; the traditional "Вафуил" comes from the Greek Old Testament's Bathouel.

decisions.choice: Слово ГОСПОДА, которое было к (L); ГОСПОДЬ обратился к (B), as Hosea 1:1; слово, которое ГОСПОДЬ дал (R)
decisions.reason: The Prophets' formula "the word of the LORD came to X" in its fixed wording per level, shaped here as the book's heading (a noun phrase at Literal).

decisions.choice: the elders: the old people of the community, who were also its leaders
decisions.reason: The word means old people and, from them, the leaders of a town or people. Here the prophet appeals to those whose memory goes back furthest: no one alive has seen anything like this. In 1:14 and 2:16 the same word is used of those gathered for the fast.

decisions.choice: the inhabitants of the land: the people of Judah
decisions.reason: The "land" here is the land of Judah, the LORD's land (1:6; 2:18), not the whole earth. The people addressed are those who live there and gather at the temple in Jerusalem (1:14).

decisions.choice: has this happened in your days or your fathers' days?: nothing like it has ever been seen
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no. It recalls the locust plague of Egypt, which neither the fathers nor the fathers' fathers of the Egyptians had seen (Exodus 10:6, 14). Joel's disaster is described as being as great as that one.

decisions.choice: your ancestors (B, R); your fathers (L)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" here means the generations before, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors". Readable says "in your lifetime" for "in your days".

decisions.choice: Ouçam ... escutem (plural imperatives, "vocês")
decisions.reason: The prophet calls a whole group, so the imperatives are the plural of "vocês" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4); the archaic "vós" forms are not used. This holds for the book's calls to the elders, priests, farmers and people.

decisions.choice: plural "you" with the plural_you setting
decisions.reason: Joel speaks to the elders and the whole people, so every plural "you" in the book is a plural_you span: ustedes forms by default, vosotros forms as the alternative. A command to one person (1:8) is tú.

decisions.choice: "조상들" at every level, with no gender span
decisions.reason: Korean "조상" covers the English "fathers" and "ancestors" alike.

decisions.choice: the prophet addresses the people as "các người"; "tổ tiên" with no gender span
decisions.reason: In chapter 1 Joel speaks in his own voice, calling the people to lament, so he uses the Isaiah note's "các người" for a prophet addressing the people; "các ngươi" stays for God's own speech. "Tổ tiên" already includes men and women.

decisions.choice: "baba zenu" (L); "babu zenu" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As Hosea 9:10 and Jeremiah 7:25: "babu" already means forebears in general, so no gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: "አባቶቻችሁ" (B), "ቅድመ አያቶቻችሁ" (R) for "your ancestors"
decisions.reason: In Amharic "አባቶች" already reads as "forefathers, ancestors", so Balanced keeps it; Readable says "ቅድመ አያቶቻችሁ", the everyday word, as the English Readable says "ancestors". No gender span is needed.

decisions.choice: पुरनिए (L); बुज़ुर्ग अगुवे (B); बुज़ुर्ग (R)
decisions.reason: The elders were the old people of the community and also its leaders (meaning decision m1); the words the earlier books use for them. The prophet addresses the people with तुम throughout.

decisions.choice: предков (B, R); отцов (L)
decisions.reason: As the English, Balanced and Readable say ancestors, since the fathers are earlier generations.

decisions.choice: tell: the one verb serves for the whole chain of generations
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the verb once and lets it carry through the next two lines: each generation is to pass the story on to the next.

decisions.choice: four names for locusts: kinds of locust, stages of its growth, or simply four names for one plague
alternatives: four stages in the growth of one kind of locust
decisions.reason: The four words are the cutting locust (from a verb meaning to cut off), the swarming locust (the most common word for locust), the hopping or licking locust, and the stripping or finishing locust (from a verb meaning to consume). They may name different kinds of locust, or the stages through which a locust grows from a crawling young insect to a flying adult, or they may be four poetic names for the same insect. In 2:25 the four names come in a different order, which suggests that they are not a strict sequence. The point is plain either way: wave after wave came until nothing was left.

decisions.choice: a real locust plague, which stripped the land
decisions.reason: Swarms of desert locusts, in numbers beyond counting, can strip every green thing from a region in hours (Exodus 10:12-15). The law names locusts among the curses on a disobedient people (Deuteronomy 28:38, 42), and Solomon prays about them (1 Kings 8:37). The rest of the chapter describes the damage to vines, fig trees, grain and pasture. Some ancient readers took the four locusts as pictures of four enemy empires; the text itself speaks of locusts, which 1:6 and chapter 2 then describe as an invading army.

decisions.choice: the cutting locust, the swarming locust, the hopping locust, the stripping locust (L, B); one swarm of locusts after another (R)
decisions.reason: The names follow the wording set for the Twelve. Literal and Balanced give each name its own English word, so the reader can follow the chain and see it come back in 2:25. Readable does not name four kinds, which might settle a question the text leaves open (m1), and says what the chain means.

decisions.choice: o gafanhoto cortador, o gafanhoto migrador, o gafanhoto saltador, o gafanhoto devorador (L, B); um enxame de gafanhotos depois do outro (R)
alternatives: a locusta, o gafanhoto, a lagarta, o pulgão
o cortador, o enxame, o saltador, o devorador
decisions.reason: For the whole book (the four names return in 2:25): as the English, each Hebrew name keeps one Portuguese word, so the reader can follow the chain. The cutter is "cortador"; the common swarming locust is "migrador", the name of the swarming kind that travels in clouds; the hopper is "saltador"; the one that finishes everything is "devorador". The old list "lagarta, pulgão" names other insects and hides that all four are locusts (m1). Readable does not name four kinds, as the English Readable.

decisions.choice: "la langosta cortadora, la langosta migratoria, la langosta saltadora, la langosta devoradora" (L, B); "una nube de langostas tras otra" (R)
decisions.reason: The four Hebrew names as the terms note sets; they may be kinds of locust or stages of growth. The same names return in 2:25.

decisions.choice: "자르는 메뚜기, 떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기, 뛰는 메뚜기, 갉아 먹는 메뚜기" (L, B); "메뚜기 떼가 잇달아" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names, describing what each does rather than using older names few readers know; whether they are kinds or stages of locust is uncertain, as the shared footnote says. Joel 2:25 repeats the list.

decisions.choice: "la sauterelle qui ronge, la sauterelle en essaim, la sauterelle qui bondit, la sauterelle qui dévaste" (L, B), "des nuées de sauterelles, l'une après l'autre" (R); the same names in 2:25
alternatives: "le gazam, l'arbeh, le yéleq, le hasil"
decisions.reason: As the term sheet: French has no four separate common words that match the Hebrew, which may name kinds or stages of locust, so each name is "sauterelle" with a description; Readable follows the English "one swarm after another".

decisions.choice: "châu chấu cắn phá", "châu chấu đàn", "châu chấu non", "cào cào ăn trụi" (L, B); "hết đàn châu chấu này đến đàn châu chấu khác" (R)
decisions.reason: The terms note's names for the four locusts (with Psalm 105:34 for yeleq and 1 Kings 8:37 for chasil), used again in 2:25; Readable says what the four names add up to, as the English Readable does. Whether they are kinds or stages is left open, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "nzige wakataji, nzige wa makundi, nzige warukaji, nzige waharibifu" (L, B); "kundi moja la nzige baada ya jingine" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's four names, made from what each Hebrew name says (cut, swarm, hop, strip), so that the kinds or stages (m1) stay apart and the line keeps clear of the Union Version's names; Readable follows the English "one swarm after another".

decisions.choice: the four locust names: gazam "ቆራጭ አንበጣ" (cutting locust), arbeh "አንበጣ" (swarming locust), yeleq "ዘላይ አንበጣ" (hopping locust), hasil "ኩብኩባ" (stripping locust); the same four words in 2:25
decisions.reason: Arbeh is the locust of the Egyptian plague and of the food laws, "አንበጣ" in Exodus 10 and Leviticus 11:22 on main; hasil is "ኩብኩባ" in 1 Kings 8:37 and 2 Chronicles 6:28 on main (and Psalm 78:46, Isaiah 33:4). For the two names found with these only in Joel and a few prophets, Amharic describes them as the English does: "ቆራጭ" (that cuts) and "ዘላይ" (that hops). Whether they are kinds or stages of the locust is open (the meaning decision), so the names stay descriptive.

decisions.choice: "የአንበጣ መንጋ አንዱ ከሌላው ቀጥሎ" (one swarm of locusts after another)
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, which does not name the four kinds.

decisions.choice: "різун", "сарана", "стрибунець", "обдирач" for the four locust names (L, B); "сарана" for the swarming locust as in Nahum 3:15
decisions.reason: The four Hebrew names describe what the insects do (cut, swarm, hop, strip), as the English names do; Ukrainian names them by the same actions. Readable speaks only of swarm after swarm, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: कुतरनेवाली टिड्डी, झुंडवाली टिड्डी, फुदकनेवाली टिड्डी, नोचनेवाली टिड्डी (L, B); टिड्डियों के दल पर दल (R)
alternatives: गाज़ाम, अर्बे, येलेक, हासील (the Hebrew names)
decisions.reason: Hindi has only टिड्डी and टिड्डा, so Literal and Balanced give each of the four names a describing word taken from the English names, keeping them apart so the chain can be followed and recognized when it returns in 2:25. Readable, like the English, speaks of swarm after swarm (meaning decision m1). Book-wide choice for Joel.

decisions.choice: грызущая, налетающая, прыгающая, пожирающая саранча (L, B); одна стая саранчи за другой (R)
decisions.reason: The four Hebrew names (gazam, arbeh, yeleq, chasil) are kept apart by an adjective each, all with "саранча", because the meaning decision leaves open whether they are kinds or stages of locust; worms and aphids would decide it. Readable, like the English, says one swarm after another. Joel 2:25 uses the same names.

records.literal_gloss: Wake up, drunkards, and weep; and wail, all drinkers of wine, over [the] sweet wine, for it has been cut off from your mouth.

en.L: Wake up, drunkards, and weep; \q and wail, all drinkers of wine, \q over the sweet wine, for it is cut off from your mouth.
en.B: Wake up, you drunkards, and weep! \q Wail, all you who drink wine, \q because the sweet wine has been cut off from your lips.
en.R: Wake up, you drunkards, and cry! \q All you who drink wine, cry out in grief, \q because there is no more sweet wine for you to drink.

pt.L: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem; \q e lamentem, todos os bebedores de vinho, \q por causa do vinho doce, porque ele foi cortado da boca de vocês.
pt.B: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem! \q Gritem de dor, todos vocês que bebem vinho, \q porque o vinho doce foi tirado dos seus lábios.
pt.R: Acordem, bêbados, e chorem! \q Todos vocês que bebem vinho, gritem de tristeza, \q porque não há mais vinho doce para vocês beberem.

es.L: {{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}; \q y {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, todos los bebedores de vino, \q por el mosto, porque se {{plural_you:les|os}} ha quitado de la boca.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, todos los que beben vino, \q porque el mosto {{plural_you:les|os}} ha sido arrebatado de los labios!
es.R: ¡{{plural_you:Despierten|Despertad}}, borrachos, y {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}}! \q Todos los que beben vino, ¡{{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor, \q porque ya no hay vino dulce para beber!

ko.L: 술 취한 자들아, 깨어나서 울어라. \q 포도주를 마시는 모든 자들아, 통곡하여라. \q 단 포도주 때문에 [울어라]. 그것이 너희 입에서 끊어졌다.
ko.B: 술 취한 자들아, 깨어나서 울어라! \q 포도주를 마시는 자들아, 모두 통곡하여라! \q 단 포도주가 너희 입술에서 끊어졌다.
ko.R: 술 취한 사람들아, 깨어나서 울어라! \q 포도주를 마시는 사람들아, 모두 슬피 울부짖어라! \q 이제는 너희가 마실 단 포도주가 없다.

fr.L: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ; \q et gémissez, vous tous, buveurs de vin, \q à cause du vin doux, car il est retranché de votre bouche.
fr.B: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ! \q Gémissez, vous tous qui buvez du vin, \q car le vin doux a été retiré de vos lèvres.
fr.R: Réveillez-vous, ivrognes, et pleurez ! \q Vous tous qui buvez du vin, criez votre chagrin, \q parce qu’il n’y a plus de vin doux à boire.

vi.L: Hãy thức dậy, hỡi những kẻ say sưa, và khóc lóc; \q hãy kêu gào, hỡi tất cả những kẻ uống rượu, \q vì rượu nho ngọt, vì nó đã bị cất khỏi miệng các người.
vi.B: Hỡi những kẻ say sưa, hãy tỉnh dậy mà khóc lóc! \q Hỡi tất cả những ai uống rượu, hãy kêu gào, \q vì rượu nho ngọt đã bị cất khỏi môi các người.
vi.R: Hỡi những kẻ say rượu, hãy thức dậy mà khóc! \q Hỡi tất cả những ai uống rượu, hãy kêu khóc thảm thiết, \q vì không còn rượu nho ngọt cho các người uống nữa.

sw.L: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie; \q ombolezeni, ninyi nyote mnywao divai, \q kwa ajili ya divai tamu, kwa maana imekatiliwa mbali na vinywa vyenu.
sw.B: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie! \q Ombolezeni, ninyi nyote mnaokunywa divai, \q kwa sababu divai tamu imeondolewa midomoni mwenu.
sw.R: Amkeni, enyi walevi, mlie! \q Ninyi nyote mnaokunywa divai, lieni kwa huzuni, \q kwa sababu hakuna tena divai tamu ya kunywa.

am.L: እናንተ ሰካራሞች፣ ንቁ፤ አልቅሱም፤ \q የወይን ጠጅ የምትጠጡ ሁሉ፣ ዋይ በሉ፤ \q ስለ ጣፋጩ የወይን ጠጅ፣ ከአፋችሁ ተቆርጧልና።
am.B: እናንተ ሰካራሞች፣ ንቁ፤ አልቅሱም! \q የወይን ጠጅ የምትጠጡ ሁሉ፣ ዋይ በሉ፤ \q ጣፋጩ የወይን ጠጅ ከከንፈራችሁ ተቆርጧልና።
am.R: እናንተ ሰካራሞች፣ ንቁና አልቅሱ! \q የወይን ጠጅ የምትጠጡ ሁሉ፣ በሐዘን ጩኹ፤ \q የምትጠጡት ጣፋጭ የወይን ጠጅ ከእንግዲህ የለምና።

hi.L: हे मतवालो, जागो और रोओ; \q और हे दाखमधु के सब पीनेवालो, हाय-हाय करो, \q मीठे दाखमधु के कारण, क्योंकि वह तुम्हारे मुँह से छीन लिया गया है।
hi.B: हे मतवालो, जागो और रोओ! \q हे दाखमधु पीनेवालो, विलाप करो, \q क्योंकि मीठा दाखमधु तुम्हारे होंठों से छिन गया है।
hi.R: हे शराबियो, जागो और रोओ! \q हे दाखमधु पीनेवालो, दुख से चिल्लाओ, \q क्योंकि अब तुम्हारे पीने के लिए मीठा दाखमधु नहीं रहा।

ru.L: Проснитесь, пьяницы, и плачьте; \q и рыдайте, все пьющие вино, \q о молодом вине, потому что оно отнято от ваших уст.
ru.B: Проснитесь, пьяницы, и плачьте! \q Рыдайте, все, кто пьёт вино, \q потому что молодое вино отнято от ваших губ.
ru.R: Проснитесь, пьяницы, и плачьте! \q Все, кто пьёт вино, кричите от горя, \q потому что больше нет для вас молодого вина.

uk.L: Прокиньтеся, пʼяниці, і плачте; \q і ридайте, усі, хто пʼє вино, \q за молодим вином, бо воно відняте від ваших уст.
uk.B: Прокиньтеся, пʼяниці, і плачте! \q Ридайте, усі, хто пʼє вино, \q бо молоде вино відняте від ваших уст.
uk.R: Прокиньтеся, пʼяниці, і плачте! \q Усі, хто пʼє вино, голосіть з горя, \q бо вам більше нема молодого вина.

decisions.choice: sweet wine: the fresh juice of newly pressed grapes
decisions.reason: The word names new, sweet wine, the juice just trodden out of the grapes (Isaiah 49:26; Amos 9:13). With the vines stripped (verse 7) there will be no grape harvest. In 4:18 the same word returns in the promise that the mountains will drip with sweet wine.

decisions.choice: wake up, drunkards: the first to feel the loss are called to wake to the disaster
decisions.reason: The call to the drunkards has a bitter edge: they are told to wake from their stupor, and they are the first to notice that the wine is gone. The call to grieve then passes to the farmers (verse 11) and the priests (verse 13).

decisions.choice: Wail (L, B); cry out in grief (R); your lips (B)
decisions.reason: The call to wail follows the wording set in Isaiah: "Wail" at Literal and Balanced, "Cry out in grief" at Readable. Balanced says "lips" for "mouth"; Readable says plainly that the wine is gone.

decisions.choice: lamentem (L); gritem de dor (B); gritem de tristeza (R); o vinho doce
decisions.reason: For the whole book, the call to wail takes the words Isaiah 13:6 uses in Portuguese: "lamentem" (L), "gritem de dor" (B), "chorem e gritem de tristeza" shortened to "gritem de tristeza" (R), as the English follows Isaiah. The other mourning verbs (1:8, 1:13) take "prantear" and "chorar de luto" so the words stay apart. The fresh juice of m1 is "vinho doce" here and in 4:18.

decisions.choice: "[[Giman|Gemid]]" (L, B); "[[lloren|llorad]] de dolor" (R)
decisions.reason: Helilu (wail) as the terms note sets for the Spanish prophets (Isaiah 13:6).

decisions.choice: "el mosto" (L, B); "vino dulce" (R)
decisions.reason: Asis, the fresh juice of the grapes, is kept apart from tirosh ("mosto" / "vino nuevo") only at Readable; at Literal and Balanced "mosto" names the sweet wine, as the published Spanish does.

decisions.choice: "ጣፋጭ የወይን ጠጅ" for sweet wine (ʿasis), here and in 4:18
decisions.reason: Isaiah 49:26 has "ጣፋጭ የወይን ጠጅ" for the same word at Literal. "አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ" is kept for tirosh (new wine) in 1:10, so the two words stay apart.

decisions.choice: हाय-हाय करो (L); विलाप करो (B); दुख से चिल्लाओ (R)
decisions.reason: The call to wail keeps the wording Isaiah uses in this translation (Isaiah 13:6), one form per level through Joel.

decisions.choice: молодое вино
decisions.reason: The sweet wine is the fresh juice of newly pressed grapes (meaning decision); "молодое вино" says it is new, not a dessert wine.

source.text: כִּֽי־גוֹי֙ עָלָ֣ה עַל־אַרְצִ֔י עָצ֖וּם וְאֵ֣ין מִסְפָּ֑ר שִׁנָּיו֙ שִׁנֵּ֣י אַרְיֵ֔ה וּֽמְתַלְּע֥וֹת לָבִ֖יא לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For a nation has come up against my land, mighty and without number; its teeth [are the] teeth of a lion, and [the] fangs of a lioness [are] to it.

en.L: For a nation has come up against {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q mighty and without number; \q its teeth [are] a lion's teeth, \q and it has the fangs of a lioness.
en.B: For a nation has invaded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land, \q powerful and too many to count. \q Its teeth are a lion's teeth; \q it has the fangs of a lioness.
en.R: A nation of locusts has invaded {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} land. \q It is powerful, and there are too many to count. \q Its teeth are like a lion's teeth. \q It has fangs like a lioness.

pt.L: Pois uma nação subiu contra a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, \q poderosa e sem número; \q os seus dentes [são] dentes de leão, \q e ela tem as presas de uma leoa.
pt.B: Pois uma nação invadiu a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra, \q poderosa e numerosa demais para se contar. \q Os seus dentes são dentes de leão; \q ela tem as presas de uma leoa.
pt.R: Uma nação de gafanhotos invadiu a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} terra. \q Ela é poderosa, e são tantos que ninguém consegue contar. \q Os seus dentes são como dentes de leão. \q Ela tem presas como as de uma leoa.

es.L: Porque una nación ha subido contra {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra, \q poderosa y sin número; \q sus dientes [son] dientes de león, \q y tiene colmillos de leona.
es.B: Porque una nación ha invadido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra, \q poderosa e incontable. \q Sus dientes son dientes de león; \q tiene colmillos de leona.
es.R: Una nación de langostas ha invadido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} tierra. \q Es poderosa, y son tantas que no se pueden contar. \q Sus dientes son como dientes de león. \q Tiene colmillos como de leona.

ko.L: 한 민족이 내 땅에 올라왔다. \q 강하고 수를 셀 수 없다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨이고, \q 그것에게는 암사자의 송곳니가 있다.
ko.B: 한 민족이 내 땅에 쳐들어왔다. \q 그들은 강하고 수가 셀 수 없이 많다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨 같고, \q 암사자의 송곳니를 가졌다.
ko.R: 메뚜기 민족이 내 땅에 쳐들어왔다. \q 그들은 강하고, 너무 많아서 셀 수도 없다. \q 그 이빨은 사자의 이빨 같다. \q 암사자처럼 날카로운 송곳니가 있다.

fr.L: Car une nation est montée contre {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays, \q puissante et sans nombre ; \q ses dents [sont] des dents de lion, \q et elle a les crocs d’une lionne.
fr.B: Car une nation a envahi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays, \q puissante et innombrable. \q Ses dents sont des dents de lion ; \q elle a les crocs d’une lionne.
fr.R: Une nation de sauterelles a envahi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} pays. \q Elle est puissante, et on ne peut pas les compter. \q Ses dents sont comme des dents de lion. \q Elle a des crocs comme une lionne.

vi.L: Vì một dân đã kéo lên đánh xứ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q mạnh mẽ và không đếm được; \q răng nó [là] răng sư tử, \q và nó có nanh của sư tử cái.
vi.B: Vì một dân đã xâm chiếm xứ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q hùng mạnh và đông vô số. \q Răng nó là răng sư tử; \q nó có nanh của sư tử cái.
vi.R: Một dân tộc châu chấu đã xâm chiếm xứ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng rất mạnh và đông không đếm xuể. \q Răng chúng như răng sư tử. \q Chúng có nanh như sư tử cái.

sw.L: Kwa maana taifa limepanda juu ya nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q lenye nguvu, lisilo na hesabu; \q meno yake [ni] meno ya simba, \q nalo lina magego ya simba jike.
sw.B: Kwa maana taifa limeivamia nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q lenye nguvu na lisilohesabika. \q Meno yake ni meno ya simba; \q lina magego ya simba jike.
sw.R: Taifa la nzige limeivamia nchi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}. \q Lina nguvu, na ni wengi mno wasiohesabika. \q Meno yake ni kama meno ya simba. \q Lina magego kama ya simba jike.

am.L: ሕዝብ በምድሬ ላይ ወጥቷልና፤ \q [እርሱም] ብርቱና ቁጥር የሌለው ነው፤ \q ጥርሶቹ የአንበሳ ጥርሶች [ናቸው]፤ \q የእንስት አንበሳም ክራንቻ አለው።
am.B: ሕዝብ ምድሬን ወሯልና፤ \q ብርቱና ሊቆጠር የማይችል ብዙ ነው። \q ጥርሶቹ የአንበሳ ጥርሶች ናቸው፤ \q የእንስት አንበሳ ክራንቻ አለው።
am.R: የአንበጣ ሕዝብ ምድሬን ወሯል። \q ብርቱ ነው፤ ቁጥሩም ሊቆጠር የማይችል ብዙ ነው። \q ጥርሶቹ እንደ አንበሳ ጥርስ ናቸው፤ \q እንደ እንስት አንበሳ ያለ ክራንቻ አለው።

hi.L: क्योंकि एक जाति मेरे देश पर चढ़ आई है, \q सामर्थी और अनगिनत; \q उसके दाँत सिंह के दाँत [हैं], \q और उसकी डाढ़ें सिंहनी की हैं।
hi.B: क्योंकि एक राष्ट्र ने मेरे देश पर चढ़ाई की है, \q शक्तिशाली और इतना बड़ा कि गिना न जा सके। \q उसके दाँत सिंह के दाँत हैं; \q उसकी डाढ़ें सिंहनी की-सी हैं।
hi.R: टिड्डियों के एक राष्ट्र ने मेरे देश पर चढ़ाई की है। \q वह शक्तिशाली है, और उसकी गिनती नहीं हो सकती। \q उसके दाँत सिंह के दाँतों जैसे हैं। \q उसकी डाढ़ें सिंहनी जैसी हैं।

ru.L: Ведь народ поднялся на {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю, \q сильный и без числа; \q зубы его — зубы льва, \q и клыки львицы у него.
ru.B: Ведь на {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю вторгся народ, \q могучий и бесчисленный. \q Его зубы — зубы льва, \q у него клыки львицы.
ru.R: На {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю напал народ — саранча. \q Он сильный, и его не сосчитать. \q Его зубы как зубы льва. \q У него клыки, как у львицы.

uk.L: Бо народ піднявся на {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю, \q могутній і без числа; \q його зуби [—] зуби лева, \q і в нього ікла левиці.
uk.B: Бо народ вдерся в {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю, \q сильний і незліченний. \q Його зуби — левові зуби; \q у нього ікла левиці.
uk.R: Народ сарани вдерся в {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю. \q Він сильний, і його не злічити. \q Його зуби, як левові зуби. \q У нього ікла, як у левиці.

decisions.choice: a nation: the locust swarm, pictured as an invading people
alternatives: a human army, foreshadowed by the locusts
decisions.reason: The word usually names a nation. Proverbs 30:25-27 calls ants and locusts "a people" in the same way. What this "nation" does in verse 7, stripping vines and fig trees, is what locusts do, so the swarm of verse 4 is meant, described as an army that invades the land. Chapter 2 develops the picture. Some readers take the nation as a human army that the locusts foreshadow.

decisions.choice: my land: the LORD speaks of the land as his own
alternatives: the prophet speaks for the people
decisions.reason: The speaker is not named. The land is called the LORD's land in 2:18 ("his land") and 4:2 ("my land"), and the vine and fig tree of verse 7 are "my" too, so the LORD most likely speaks here. The prophet may instead be speaking for the people, who would call it "my land" as well.

decisions.choice: teeth of a lion, fangs of a lioness: small insects that devour like the fiercest of animals
decisions.reason: Two words for the lion are used; the second may mean a lioness. A locust's jaws are tiny, but together the swarm devours as a lion tears its prey. Revelation 9:8 takes up the picture for its locusts.

decisions.choice: A nation of locusts
decisions.reason: Readable says that the nation is the locusts (m1), since a young reader would otherwise think of a human army.

decisions.choice: "내 땅": God speaks here, in 해라체 with no honorific
decisions.reason: As the shared decision says, the LORD speaks of the land as his own (1:6–7); the rest of the chapter is the prophet's voice, where God takes -시-.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun span on "yangu" (my land)
decisions.reason: The LORD speaks of the land as his own (m2), so the free possessive takes the span, as the English "my" does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in the Amharic of Joel 1.
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God has nothing to change in Amharic; pronouns and verb forms for God are written plainly.

decisions.choice: goy as "ሕዝብ" (a nation, a people) for the locust swarm
decisions.reason: The swarm is pictured as one invading people; the plural "nations" of 2:17, 19 and chapter 4 is "ሕዝቦች". Readable makes the picture plain with "የአንበጣ ሕዝብ", as the English does.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Hindi
decisions.reason: The English marks God's pronouns ("my land") with the deity_pronoun setting. Devanagari has no capital letters, so the Hindi has no such spans; respect for God is carried by the honorific third person (वे, उनका). This holds for every file of Joel.

decisions.choice: जाति (L); राष्ट्र (B, R)
decisions.reason: The locust swarm is pictured as an invading people (meaning decision m1). Literal says जाति, as for goy elsewhere; Balanced and Readable say राष्ट्र, since जाति also means caste and देश would clash with "my land" in the same line.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} землю
decisions.reason: God speaks of the land as his own; his first-person pronouns carry the deity_pronoun setting through the book, as in Isaiah (not on a reflexive or a sentence-initial Я).

decisions.choice: народ — саранча
decisions.reason: As the English Readable, the locusts are named, since the nation is the swarm (meaning decision).

source.text: שָׂ֤ם גַּפְנִי֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה וּתְאֵנָתִ֖י לִקְצָפָ֑ה חָשֹׂ֤ף חֲשָׂפָהּ֙ וְהִשְׁלִ֔יךְ הִלְבִּ֖ינוּ שָׂרִיגֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: It has made my vine into a waste, and my fig tree into splinters; stripping it has stripped it and thrown [it] down; white have become its branches.

en.L: It has made {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vine a waste \q and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig tree a splintered stump; \q it has stripped off its bark and thrown it down; \q its branches have turned white.
en.B: It has laid waste {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} vines \q and turned {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig trees to broken stumps. \q It has stripped off their bark and thrown it down, \q and their branches are left white.
en.R: It has ruined {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} grapevines \q and torn {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fig trees to pieces. \q It has stripped off their bark and thrown it away. \q Now their branches are white and bare.

pt.L: Ela fez da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} videira uma desolação \q e da {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} figueira um toco lascado; \q descascou-a inteiramente e [a] lançou por terra; \q os seus ramos ficaram brancos.
pt.B: Ela devastou as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} videiras \q e reduziu as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} figueiras a tocos quebrados. \q Arrancou a casca delas e a jogou fora, \q e os seus ramos ficaram brancos.
pt.R: Ela destruiu as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} parreiras \q e despedaçou as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} figueiras. \q Arrancou a casca delas e a jogou longe. \q Agora os seus galhos estão brancos e nus.

es.L: Ha convertido {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vid en desolación \q y {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} higuera en astillas; \q del todo la ha descortezado y [la] ha derribado; \q sus ramas se han vuelto blancas.
es.B: Ha arrasado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} viñas \q y ha dejado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} higueras hechas astillas. \q Les ha arrancado la corteza y la ha tirado al suelo, \q y sus ramas han quedado blancas.
es.R: Ha arruinado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} viñas \q y ha despedazado {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} higueras. \q Les ha arrancado la corteza y la ha tirado. \q Ahora sus ramas están blancas y desnudas.

ko.L: 그것이 내 포도나무를 황폐하게 하고, \q 내 무화과나무를 부러진 그루터기로 만들었다. \q 그 껍질을 다 벗겨 내던지니, \q 그 가지들이 하얗게 되었다.
ko.B: 그것이 내 포도나무를 망쳐 놓고, \q 내 무화과나무를 부러진 그루터기로 만들었다. \q 껍질을 벗겨 내던져 버리니, \q 가지들이 하얗게 드러났다.
ko.R: 그것들이 내 포도나무를 망쳐 놓았다. \q 내 무화과나무를 갈기갈기 찢어 놓았다. \q 껍질을 벗겨 내버렸다. \q 이제 가지들은 하얗게 벗겨져 앙상하다.

fr.L: Elle a fait de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} vigne une désolation \q et de {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} figuier un tronc brisé ; \q elle l’a entièrement écorcé et l’a jeté à terre ; \q ses branches sont devenues blanches.
fr.B: Elle a ravagé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} vignes \q et réduit {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} figuiers à des troncs brisés. \q Elle a arraché leur écorce et l’a jetée à terre, \q et leurs branches restent toutes blanches.
fr.R: Elle a détruit {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} vignes \q et mis {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} figuiers en pièces. \q Elle a arraché leur écorce et l’a jetée. \q Maintenant leurs branches sont blanches et nues.

vi.L: Nó đã làm cho cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành hoang phế \q và cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành gốc gãy vụn; \q nó đã lột trụi vỏ và quăng đi; \q các cành của nó đã trở nên trắng bệch.
vi.B: Nó đã tàn phá các cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và biến các cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} thành những gốc gãy. \q Nó đã lột sạch vỏ cây và quăng đi, \q để lại những cành trắng bệch.
vi.R: Chúng đã phá hại các cây nho của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q và xé nát các cây vả của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Chúng đã lột sạch vỏ cây rồi vứt đi. \q Bây giờ các cành cây trắng bệch và trơ trụi.

sw.L: Limeufanya mzabibu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} ukiwa \q na mtini {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} kisiki kilichovunjika; \q limeubambua kabisa na kuutupa chini; \q matawi yake yamekuwa meupe.
sw.B: Limeiharibu mizabibu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q na kuigeuza mitini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} kuwa visiki vilivyovunjika. \q Limebambua magome yake na kuyatupa chini, \q na matawi yake yamebaki meupe.
sw.R: Limeiharibu mizabibu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} \q na kuirarua mitini {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} vipande vipande. \q Limebambua magome yake na kuyatupa mbali. \q Sasa matawi yake ni meupe, hayana kitu.

am.L: ወይኔን ባድማ፣ \q በለሴንም የተሰባበረ ጉቶ አደረገ፤ \q ቅርፊቱን ፈጽሞ ገፈፈው፤ ጣለውም፤ \q ቅርንጫፎቹም ነጡ።
am.B: ወይኖቼን አጠፋ፤ \q በለሶቼንም ቆራርጦ ጉቶ አደረጋቸው። \q ቅርፊታቸውን ገፍፎ ጣለው፤ \q ቅርንጫፎቻቸውም ነጥተው ቀሩ።
am.R: የወይን ተክሎቼን አበላሸ፤ \q በለሶቼንም ቆራረጣቸው። \q ቅርፊታቸውን ገፍፎ ጣለው። \q አሁን ቅርንጫፎቻቸው ነጥተው ተራቁተዋል።

hi.L: उसने मेरी दाखलता को उजाड़ \q और मेरे अंजीर के पेड़ को ठूँठ बना दिया है; \q उसने उसकी छाल पूरी तरह छील डाली और फेंक दी है; \q उसकी डालियाँ सफ़ेद हो गई हैं।
hi.B: उसने मेरी दाखलताओं को उजाड़ दिया है \q और मेरे अंजीर के पेड़ों को टूटे हुए ठूँठ बना दिया है। \q उसने उनकी छाल छीलकर फेंक दी है, \q और उनकी डालियाँ सफ़ेद रह गई हैं।
hi.R: उसने मेरी अंगूर की बेलें बरबाद कर दी हैं \q और मेरे अंजीर के पेड़ों को टुकड़े-टुकड़े कर दिया है। \q उसने उनकी छाल उतारकर फेंक दी है। \q अब उनकी डालियाँ सफ़ेद और नंगी हैं।

ru.L: Он превратил {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} лозу в пустошь \q и {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} смоковницу — в обломки; \q ободрал с неё [кору] догола и бросил, \q побелели её ветви.
ru.B: Он опустошил {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} виноградники \q и превратил {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} смоковницы в обломанные пни. \q Он ободрал с них кору и бросил её, \q и их ветви остались белыми.
ru.R: Он погубил {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} виноградные лозы \q и изломал {{deity_pronoun:мои|Мои}} смоковницы. \q Он ободрал с них кору и выбросил её. \q Теперь их ветви белые и голые.

uk.L: Він обернув {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} лозу на пустку \q і {{deity_pronoun:мою|Мою}} смоковницю на трісок; \q обдер з неї кору й кинув; \q побіліли її гілки.
uk.B: Він спустошив {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} лози \q і обернув {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} смоковниці на зламані пні. \q Він обдер з них кору й кинув її, \q і їхні гілки залишилися білими.
uk.R: Він знищив {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} виноградні лози \q і пошматував {{deity_pronoun:мої|Мої}} інжирні дерева. \q Він обдер з них кору й викинув її. \q Тепер їхні гілки білі й голі.

decisions.choice: vine and fig tree: the main fruit crops, and a picture of the people's life in the land
decisions.reason: The vine and the fig tree stand for a settled, peaceful life in the land (1 Kings 5:5; Micah 4:4) and are sometimes pictures of Israel itself (Hosea 9:10). When the leaves and fruit are gone, locusts gnaw the bark, and the branches are left bare and white.

decisions.choice: a splintered stump: a rare word, perhaps for something snapped off
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It comes from a root that may mean to snap or break off, so it pictures fig trees snapped and splintered, or perhaps their bark peeled into shreds.

decisions.choice: my vine, my fig tree: the LORD's, as in verse 6
decisions.reason: The "my" continues verse 6: the land and its vines and trees belong to the LORD (see the note there).

decisions.choice: vines, fig trees (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the singular for the whole crop. Balanced and Readable use the plural, which says the same thing in natural English; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: a minha / as minhas with the deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: "Ela" in verses 6-7 is the nation, a feminine noun in Portuguese, so the swarm is "ela" where the English says "it". The possessive "minha(s)" agrees with the vine and fig trees and takes the deity_pronoun span, as the English "my" (m3).

decisions.choice: смоковница
decisions.reason: Fig tree as the New Testament has it (смоковница at L and B); Readable keeps it here too, since the tree is named beside the vine as a pair.

source.text: אֱלִ֕י כִּבְתוּלָ֥ה חֲגֻֽרַת־שַׂ֖ק עַל־בַּ֥עַל נְעוּרֶֽיהָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Lament like a virgin girded [with] sackcloth for [the] husband of her youth.

en.L: Lament like a virgin wearing sackcloth \q for the husband of her youth.
en.B: Mourn like a young woman dressed in sackcloth, \q grieving for the man she was pledged to marry.
en.R: Cry like a young woman wearing sackcloth \q because the man she was going to marry has died.

pt.L: Pranteia como uma virgem cingida de pano de saco \q pelo marido da sua juventude.
pt.B: Chora de luto como uma moça vestida de pano de saco, \q que lamenta o noivo com quem ia se casar.
pt.R: Chora como uma moça vestida de pano de saco \q porque o homem com quem ela ia se casar morreu.

es.L: Lamenta como una virgen ceñida de cilicio \q por el esposo de su juventud.
es.B: Llora como una joven vestida de cilicio \q que se lamenta por el hombre con quien iba a casarse.
es.R: Llora como una joven vestida con ropa áspera de luto \q porque murió el hombre con quien se iba a casar.

ko.L: 너는 굵은 베옷을 두른 처녀가 \q 젊은 날의 남편을 [잃고] 슬퍼하듯 애곡하여라.
ko.B: 약혼한 남자를 잃고 슬퍼하는 처녀처럼, \q 굵은 베옷을 입고 애곡하여라.
ko.R: 결혼하기로 한 남자가 죽어서 \q 굵은 베옷을 입고 우는 젊은 여자처럼 울어라.

fr.L: Lamente-toi comme une vierge vêtue d’un sac \q pour le mari de sa jeunesse.
fr.B: Pleure comme une jeune femme vêtue d’un sac, \q en deuil de l’homme qui lui était promis.
fr.R: Pleure comme une jeune femme habillée d’un sac de deuil \q parce que l’homme qu’elle allait épouser est mort.

vi.L: Hãy than khóc như trinh nữ mặc vải thô \q vì người chồng thời son trẻ của mình.
vi.B: Hãy than khóc như thiếu nữ mặc vải thô, \q khóc thương người đã hứa hôn với mình.
vi.R: Hãy khóc như một thiếu nữ mặc vải thô \q vì người sắp cưới của mình đã chết.

sw.L: Omboleza kama bikira aliyejifunga gunia \q kwa ajili ya mume wa ujana wake.
sw.B: Omboleza kama msichana aliyevaa gunia, \q akimlilia mchumba wake.
sw.R: Lia kama msichana aliyevaa gunia \q kwa sababu mchumba wake amekufa.

am.L: ማቅ እንደ ታጠቀች ድንግል አልቅሺ፤ \q ስለ ወጣትነቷ ባል [እንደምታለቅስ]።
am.B: ማቅ ለብሳ \q ልታገባው ለታጨችው ሰው እንደምታዝን ወጣት ሴት አልቅሺ።
am.R: ማቅ እንደ ለበሰች ወጣት ሴት አልቅሺ። \q ልታገባው የነበረው ሰው ሞቶባት ታለቅሳለች።

hi.L: टाट बाँधे हुए कुँवारी के समान विलाप करो, \q जो अपनी जवानी के पति के लिए [रोती है]।
hi.B: टाट ओढ़े उस युवती के समान शोक करो, \q जो उस पुरुष के लिए रोती है जिससे उसकी सगाई हुई थी।
hi.R: टाट पहने हुए उस युवती की तरह रोओ, \q जिसका होनेवाला पति मर गया है।

ru.L: Плачь, как девица, препоясанная вретищем, \q о муже своей юности.
ru.B: Скорби, как молодая женщина, одетая в мешковину, \q оплакивающая того, с кем была обручена.
ru.R: Плачь, как девушка в одежде из мешковины, \q потому что умер её жених.

uk.L: Голоси, як діва, підперезана мішковиною, \q за чоловіком своєї юності.
uk.B: Плач, як молода жінка, вбрана в мішковину, \q що оплакує чоловіка, з яким була заручена.
uk.R: Плач, як молода жінка в мішковині, \q бо помер чоловік, за якого вона мала вийти заміж.

decisions.choice: lament: a command to one woman, the land or people pictured as a mourning bride
decisions.reason: The verb is a feminine singular command, and the word is found only here. The one addressed is not named: it is most likely the land, or Zion and its people, pictured as a woman in mourning.

decisions.choice: a virgin ... the husband of her youth: a young woman whose bridegroom has died before the marriage was complete
alternatives: a young wife mourning her husband
decisions.reason: The word for the woman names a young woman of marriageable age who has not yet married. In Israel a man pledged to marry a woman was already called her husband (Deuteronomy 22:23-24). So the picture is most likely of a young bride whose promised husband has died before the wedding. Others read it of a young wife whose husband has died.

decisions.choice: sackcloth: rough cloth worn in mourning
decisions.reason: Sackcloth was coarse cloth, often of goat's hair, worn next to the skin by those in mourning or in deep distress (Genesis 37:34; 2 Samuel 3:31).

decisions.choice: a young woman (B, R); the man she was pledged to marry (B); the man she was going to marry has died (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "virgin" and "the husband of her youth". Balanced and Readable say what the picture means (m2). Readable says plainly that he has died, which the mourning implies.

decisions.choice: Pranteia (L); Chora de luto (B); Chora (R): singular "tu" imperative
decisions.reason: The command is to one woman, the land or Zion pictured as a mourning bride (m1), so Portuguese uses the singular imperative of "tu", as God's word does to Zion or a city addressed as one. "Pano de saco" is the sackcloth of Isaiah's Portuguese.

decisions.choice: "Lamenta" / "Llora" (tú, feminine)
decisions.reason: The command is to one woman, the land or people pictured as a mourning bride, so Spanish uses tú.

decisions.choice: "cilicio" (L, B); "ropa áspera de luto" (R)
decisions.reason: Sackcloth as the terms note sets for the Spanish prophets.

decisions.choice: "굵은 베옷" for sackcloth
decisions.reason: The published prophets' word for the rough cloth of mourning.

decisions.choice: "Lamente-toi", "Pleure": singular "tu"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is to one woman, the land or people pictured as a bride in mourning; French keeps the singular, which English cannot show.

decisions.choice: "vải thô"
decisions.reason: The Isaiah and Jeremiah note's word for sackcloth, used again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: "mchumba wake" (her betrothed)
decisions.reason: The "husband of her youth" is the man she was pledged to (m2); Swahili "mchumba" names exactly that. Literal keeps "mume wa ujana wake".

decisions.choice: the feminine singular "አልቅሺ" (lament, to one woman)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew command is feminine singular: the land or the people is addressed as one mourning young woman (the meaning decision). Amharic marks this in the verb, as the Hebrew does.

decisions.choice: कुँवारी ... अपनी जवानी का पति (L); युवती ... जिससे उसकी सगाई हुई थी (B); होनेवाला पति (R)
decisions.reason: The picture is of a young woman whose bridegroom died before the marriage was complete (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the Hebrew words; Balanced and Readable say what the picture means, as the English does. The command is to one woman, the land; Hindi says विलाप करो, the form used for the people throughout.

decisions.choice: вретище (L); мешковина (B, R)
decisions.reason: Sackcloth, the rough cloth of mourning: the older word at Literal, plain "мешковина" at Balanced and Readable.

decisions.choice: того, с кем была обручена (B); умер её жених (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: a bride whose bridegroom died before the marriage was complete.

source.text: הָכְרַ֥ת מִנְחָ֛ה וָנֶ֖סֶךְ מִבֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה אָֽבְלוּ֙ הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Has been cut off grain offering and drink offering from [the] house of Yahweh; mourn the priests, ministers of Yahweh.

en.L: Grain offering and drink offering are cut off from the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; \q the priests mourn, \q the ministers of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: Grain offerings and drink offerings have ceased in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The priests grieve, \q those who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: There is no more grain or wine to offer in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q The priests who serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} are mourning.

pt.L: Foram cortadas a oferta de cereal e a oferta de bebida da casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}; \q os sacerdotes estão de luto, \q os ministros {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}.
pt.B: As ofertas de cereal e as ofertas de bebida cessaram na casa {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q Os sacerdotes estão de luto, \q os que servem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}.
pt.R: Não há mais cereal nem vinho para oferecer no templo {{divine_name:do SENHOR|de Javé}}. \q Os sacerdotes que servem {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} estão de luto.

es.L: Han sido cortadas la ofrenda de cereal y la libación de la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}; \q los sacerdotes están de luto, \q los ministros {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}.
es.B: Las ofrendas de cereal y las libaciones han cesado en la casa {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Los sacerdotes están de luto, \q los que sirven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}.
es.R: Ya no hay grano ni vino para ofrecer en el templo {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}. \q Los sacerdotes que sirven {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} están de luto.

ko.L: 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 끊어졌다. \q 제사장들, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 자들이 슬퍼한다.
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 집에서 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 끊어졌다. \q 제사장들이 슬퍼한다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 자들이 슬퍼한다.
ko.R: 이제 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 성전에 바칠 곡식도 포도주도 없다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기는 제사장들이 슬퍼하고 있다.

fr.L: L’offrande végétale et la libation sont retranchées de la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} ; \q les prêtres sont en deuil, \q les serviteurs {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}.
fr.B: Les offrandes végétales et les libations ont cessé dans la maison {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Les prêtres sont dans le deuil, \q ceux qui servent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}.
fr.R: Il n’y a plus de grain ni de vin à offrir dans le temple {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}. \q Les prêtres qui servent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} sont en deuil.

vi.L: Tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã bị cất khỏi nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}; \q các thầy tế lễ than khóc, \q là những người phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.B: Tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã dứt khỏi nhà của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Các thầy tế lễ sầu não, \q những người phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}.
vi.R: Không còn ngũ cốc hay rượu để dâng trong đền thờ của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Các thầy tế lễ phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đang than khóc.

sw.L: Sadaka ya nafaka na sadaka ya kinywaji zimekatiliwa mbali na nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}; \q makuhani wanaomboleza, \q watumishi wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.B: Sadaka za nafaka na sadaka za kinywaji zimekoma katika nyumba ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Makuhani wanahuzunika, \q wale wanaomtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}.
sw.R: Hakuna tena nafaka wala divai ya kutoa sadaka katika hekalu la {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Makuhani wanaomtumikia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wanaomboleza.

am.L: የእህል ቁርባንና የመጠጥ ቁርባን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ቤት ተቆርጧል፤ \q ካህናቱ ያዝናሉ፤ \q {{divine_name:የእግዚአብሔር|የያህዌ}} አገልጋዮች።
am.B: የእህል ቁርባንና የመጠጥ ቁርባን {{divine_name:ከእግዚአብሔር|ከያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስ ቀርቷል። \q ካህናቱ፣ \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} የሚያገለግሉት፣ ያዝናሉ።
am.R: {{divine_name:በእግዚአብሔር|በያህዌ}} ቤተ መቅደስ የሚቀርብ እህልም ሆነ የወይን ጠጅ የለም። \q {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔርን|ያህዌን}} የሚያገለግሉ ካህናት ያዝናሉ።

hi.L: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के भवन से अन्नबलि और अर्घ कट गए हैं; \q याजक शोक करते हैं, \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के सेवक।
hi.B: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के भवन में अन्नबलि और अर्घ बंद हो गए हैं। \q याजक शोक मना रहे हैं, \q वे जो {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की सेवा करते हैं।
hi.R: {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} के मंदिर में चढ़ाने के लिए अब न अनाज रहा, न दाखमधु। \q {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} की सेवा करनेवाले याजक शोक मना रहे हैं।

ru.L: Отнято хлебное приношение и возлияние от дома {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}; \q скорбят священники, \q служители {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}.
ru.B: Прекратились хлебные приношения и возлияния в доме {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}}. \q Скорбят священники, \q служащие {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}.
ru.R: Нечего больше приносить в храм {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Яхве}} — ни зерна, ни вина. \q Священники, которые служат {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Яхве}}, плачут.

uk.L: Відняті хлібна жертва й жертва ливна від дому {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}; \q сумують священники, \q служителі {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}.
uk.B: Хлібні жертви й жертви ливні припинилися в домі {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}}. \q Сумують священники, \q ті, хто служить {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Ягве}}.
uk.R: У храмі {{divine_name:ГОСПОДА|Ягве}} більше нема ні зерна, ні вина для жертви. \q Священники, які служать {{divine_name:ГОСПОДУ|Ягве}}, сумують.

decisions.choice: grain offering and drink offering: the daily gifts offered with the morning and evening sacrifice
decisions.reason: Every morning and evening a lamb was offered with flour mixed with oil and with a drink offering of wine (Exodus 29:38-42; Numbers 28:3-8). With no grain, oil or wine, these daily offerings stop, and the regular worship of the temple is cut off.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The temple is called the LORD's house throughout the Old Testament. Joel speaks of it as standing and in use (1:13-14, 16; 2:17).

decisions.choice: ministers of the LORD: those who serve him
decisions.reason: The word means those who serve or attend on someone. It is used for the priests and Levites who served at the altar (Exodus 28:43; Jeremiah 33:21).

decisions.choice: no more grain or wine to offer in the temple
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two offerings were made of, and "temple" for "the house of the LORD".

decisions.choice: a oferta de cereal, a oferta de bebida
decisions.reason: The two offerings (m1) take the Pentateuch's words (docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md; Numbers 15:5): "oferta de cereal" and "oferta de bebida". "Libação" is the technical word, but few readers know it.

decisions.choice: "ofrenda de cereal"; "libación" (L, B)
decisions.reason: The names of the offerings as published in the Spanish Pentateuch; Readable says what was offered, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "곡식 제물", "부어 드리는 제물"
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch's plain wording for the grain and drink offerings, rather than the older Sino-Korean terms.

decisions.choice: "tế lễ ngũ cốc", "lễ quán"
decisions.reason: The offerings as published in the Pentateuch; used again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: minḥah "የእህል ቁርባን", nesekh "የመጠጥ ቁርባን"; the house of the LORD "የእግዚአብሔር ቤት" (L), "ቤተ መቅደስ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The offering words are those of Numbers 15 and 28 on main; "the house of the LORD" follows the Kings list (ቤት at Literal, ቤተ መቅደስ at Balanced and Readable).

decisions.choice: अन्नबलि और अर्घ; {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} का भवन (L, B), मंदिर (R)
decisions.reason: The grain offering and drink offering keep the words Isaiah uses (Isaiah 57:6); "the house of the LORD" is भवन at Literal and Balanced and मंदिर at Readable, as Isaiah 2:2. Readable names what the offerings were made of, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: хлебное приношение и возлияние
decisions.reason: The Pentateuch's terms for the grain offering and the drink offering.

source.text: שֻׁדַּ֣ד שָׂדֶ֔ה אָבְלָ֖ה אֲדָמָ֑ה כִּ֚י שֻׁדַּ֣ד דָּגָ֔ן הוֹבִ֥ישׁ תִּיר֖וֹשׁ אֻמְלַ֥ל יִצְהָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Devastated [is the] field; mourns [the] ground; for devastated [is the] grain, dried up [the] new wine, fails [the] fresh oil.

en.L: The field is devastated; the ground mourns, \q for the grain is devastated, \q the new wine has dried up, the fresh oil fails.
en.B: The fields are laid waste; the ground is in mourning, \q for the grain is ruined, \q the new wine has dried up, and the olive oil has failed.
en.R: The fields are ruined, and the ground itself mourns. \q The grain is destroyed. \q There is no new wine and no olive oil.

pt.L: O campo está devastado; o solo está de luto, \q porque o cereal está devastado, \q o vinho novo secou, o azeite fresco definha.
pt.B: Os campos foram arrasados; a terra está de luto, \q porque o cereal foi destruído, \q o vinho novo secou, e o azeite acabou.
pt.R: Os campos estão arruinados, e a própria terra está de luto. \q O cereal foi destruído. \q Não há vinho novo nem azeite.

es.L: El campo está devastado; la tierra está de luto, \q porque el grano está devastado, \q el mosto se ha secado, el aceite fresco se acaba.
es.B: Los campos están arrasados; la tierra está de luto, \q porque el grano está arruinado, \q el vino nuevo se ha secado y el aceite de oliva se ha agotado.
es.R: Los campos están arruinados, y la tierra misma está de luto. \q El grano está destruido. \q No hay vino nuevo ni aceite de oliva.

ko.L: 밭이 황폐해졌고 땅이 슬퍼한다. \q 곡식이 황폐해졌고, \q 새 포도주가 말랐고, 햇기름이 다했다.
ko.B: 밭은 황폐해지고 땅은 통곡한다. \q 곡식이 다 망가졌고, \q 새 포도주가 말라 버렸고, 기름이 떨어졌다.
ko.R: 밭은 망가지고 땅마저 슬퍼한다. \q 곡식이 다 없어졌다. \q 새 포도주도 없고 올리브기름도 없다.

fr.L: Le champ est dévasté ; le sol est en deuil, \q car le blé est dévasté, \q le vin nouveau est tari, l’huile fraîche manque.
fr.B: Les champs sont ravagés ; la terre est en deuil, \q car le blé est détruit, \q le vin nouveau est tari et l’huile d’olive fait défaut.
fr.R: Les champs sont ruinés, et la terre elle-même est en deuil. \q Le blé est détruit. \q Il n’y a plus de vin nouveau ni d’huile d’olive.

vi.L: Đồng ruộng bị tàn phá; đất than khóc, \q vì ngũ cốc bị tàn phá, \q rượu mới đã khô cạn, dầu mới đã cạn kiệt.
vi.B: Đồng ruộng bị tàn phá; đất đai sầu thảm, \q vì ngũ cốc đã hư hại, \q rượu mới đã khô cạn, và dầu ô-liu đã cạn kiệt.
vi.R: Đồng ruộng bị tàn phá, chính đất đai cũng than khóc. \q Ngũ cốc đã bị hủy hoại. \q Không còn rượu mới, cũng không còn dầu ô-liu.

sw.L: Shamba limeharibiwa; ardhi inaomboleza, \q kwa maana nafaka imeharibiwa, \q divai mpya imekauka, mafuta mapya yamepungua.
sw.B: Mashamba yameharibiwa; ardhi iko katika maombolezo, \q kwa maana nafaka imeharibika, \q divai mpya imekauka, na mafuta ya zeituni yamekwisha.
sw.R: Mashamba yameharibiwa, na ardhi yenyewe inaomboleza. \q Nafaka imeangamizwa. \q Hakuna divai mpya wala mafuta ya zeituni.

am.L: ሜዳው ጠፍቷል፤ መሬቱ ያዝናል፤ \q እህሉ ጠፍቷልና፤ \q አዲሱ የወይን ጠጅ ደርቋል፤ ዘይቱም አልቋል።
am.B: እርሻዎቹ ባድማ ሆነዋል፤ መሬቱ በሐዘን ላይ ነው፤ \q እህሉ ጠፍቷልና፤ \q አዲሱ የወይን ጠጅ ደርቋል፤ የወይራ ዘይቱም አልቋል።
am.R: እርሻዎቹ ጠፍተዋል፤ መሬቱም ራሱ ያዝናል። \q እህሉ ጠፍቷል። \q አዲስ የወይን ጠጅም ሆነ የወይራ ዘይት የለም።

hi.L: खेत उजड़ गया है; भूमि शोक करती है, \q क्योंकि अनाज नष्ट हो गया है, \q नया दाखमधु सूख गया है, ताज़ा तेल घट गया है।
hi.B: खेत उजड़ गए हैं; भूमि शोक में है, \q क्योंकि अनाज नष्ट हो गया है, \q नया दाखमधु सूख गया है, और जैतून का तेल ख़त्म हो गया है।
hi.R: खेत बरबाद हो गए हैं, और भूमि भी शोक कर रही है। \q अनाज नष्ट हो गया है। \q न नया दाखमधु रहा, न जैतून का तेल।

ru.L: Опустошено поле, скорбит земля, \q потому что опустошено зерно, \q высохло молодое вино, иссякло масло.
ru.B: Поля опустошены, земля в трауре, \q потому что погибло зерно, \q высохло молодое вино и иссякло оливковое масло.
ru.R: Поля разорены, и сама земля скорбит. \q Зерно погибло. \q Нет ни молодого вина, ни оливкового масла.

uk.L: Спустошене поле; сумує земля, \q бо спустошене збіжжя, \q висохло молоде вино, зникла свіжа олія.
uk.B: Поля спустошені; земля в жалобі, \q бо збіжжя знищене, \q молоде вино висохло, а оливкова олія зникла.
uk.R: Поля знищені, і сама земля сумує. \q Збіжжя загинуло. \q Нема ні молодого вина, ні оливкової олії.

decisions.choice: the ground mourns: grieves, and also dries up
decisions.reason: Two Hebrew verbs sound the same: one means to mourn, the other to dry up. Here the ground "mourns" just after the priests mourn (verse 9), and the drying of the crops follows. The word may be chosen to carry both: the parched ground looks like a mourner.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and fresh oil: the three great products of the land
decisions.reason: These are the gifts the LORD promised to a faithful people (Deuteronomy 7:13; 11:14), and their loss is among the curses of Deuteronomy 28:38-40, 51. Hosea 2:10-11 names the same three. "New wine" is freshly pressed wine; "fresh oil" is newly pressed olive oil. The Hebrew of the first line also plays on sound: "devastated" and "field" begin alike.

decisions.choice: olive oil (B, R); fresh oil (L)
decisions.reason: As in Hosea 2:10, Literal says "fresh oil" and Balanced and Readable "olive oil". Readable puts the three losses simply, and keeps "mourns" (m1).

decisions.choice: o azeite fresco (L); o azeite (B, R)
decisions.reason: Portuguese "azeite" already means olive oil, so Balanced and Readable say it in one word where the English says "olive oil"; Literal adds "fresco" for the freshly pressed oil, as Deuteronomy 11:14 names the same three gifts ("o teu cereal, o teu vinho novo e o teu azeite fresco"); this holds for 2:19 and 2:24.

decisions.choice: "el grano, el mosto, el aceite fresco" (L); "el grano, el vino nuevo, el aceite de oliva" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests in the words of the Spanish Deuteronomy 11:14, as in Hosea 2:10.

decisions.choice: "곡식, 새 포도주, 햇기름" (L), "…기름" (B), "…올리브기름" (R)
decisions.reason: The three harvests worded as in Hosea 2:10.

decisions.choice: grain, new wine and fresh oil: "እህል", "አዲስ የወይን ጠጅ", "ዘይት" (L) / "የወይራ ዘይት" (B, R), here and in 2:19, 24
decisions.reason: The three goods of the land as Deuteronomy 11:14 on main has them.

decisions.choice: नया दाखमधु; ताज़ा तेल (L), जैतून का तेल (B, R)
decisions.reason: The three products of the land (meaning decision m2) in the words Proverbs 3:10 uses for new wine; the oil is fresh oil at Literal and olive oil at Balanced and Readable, as the English. Same through Joel.

decisions.choice: опустошено ... опустошено
decisions.reason: Literal repeats one verb for field and grain, as the Hebrew does.

source.text: הֹבִ֣ישׁוּ אִכָּרִ֗ים הֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ כֹּֽרְמִ֔ים עַל־חִטָּ֖ה וְעַל־שְׂעֹרָ֑ה כִּ֥י אָבַ֖ד קְצִ֥יר שָׂדֶֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vinedressers, over wheat and over barley; for has perished [the] harvest of [the] field.

en.L: Be ashamed, farmers; wail, vinedressers, \q over the wheat and over the barley, \q for the harvest of the field has perished.
en.B: Be dismayed, you farmers! Wail, you who tend the vines, \q over the wheat and the barley, \q because the harvest of the field is lost.
en.R: Farmers, be sad and dismayed! You who grow grapes, cry out in grief! \q Cry for the wheat and the barley, \q because the harvest in the fields is ruined.

pt.L: Envergonhem-se, lavradores; lamentem, vinhateiros, \q pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque pereceu a colheita do campo.
pt.B: Fiquem consternados, agricultores! Gritem de dor, vocês que cuidam das videiras, \q pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque a colheita do campo se perdeu.
pt.R: Agricultores, fiquem tristes e desanimados! Vocês que plantam uvas, gritem de tristeza! \q Chorem pelo trigo e pela cevada, \q porque a colheita dos campos foi arruinada.

es.L: {{plural_you:Avergüéncense|Avergonzaos}}, labradores; {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, viñadores, \q por el trigo y por la cebada, \q porque se ha perdido la cosecha del campo.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Desaliéntense|Desalentaos}}, labradores! ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, los que cuidan las viñas, \q por el trigo y la cebada, \q porque la cosecha del campo se ha perdido!
es.R: ¡Labradores, {{plural_you:pónganse|poneos}} tristes y desalentados! ¡{{plural_you:Ustedes que cultivan|Vosotros que cultiváis}} uvas, {{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor! \q {{plural_you:Lloren|Llorad}} por el trigo y la cebada, \q porque la cosecha de los campos se ha arruinado.

ko.L: 농부들아, 부끄러워하여라. 포도원 일꾼들아, 통곡하여라. \q 밀과 보리 때문에 [통곡하여라]. \q 밭의 추수가 망했기 때문이다.
ko.B: 농부들아, 낙심하여라! 포도원을 가꾸는 자들아, 통곡하여라! \q 밀과 보리 때문에 울어라. \q 밭에서 거둘 것이 없어졌다.
ko.R: 농부들아, 슬퍼하고 낙심하여라! 포도를 기르는 사람들아, 슬피 울부짖어라! \q 밀과 보리를 두고 울어라. \q 밭에서 거둘 곡식이 다 망가졌다.

fr.L: Soyez honteux, laboureurs ; gémissez, vignerons, \q à cause du froment et de l’orge, \q car la moisson des champs a péri.
fr.B: Soyez consternés, laboureurs ! Gémissez, vignerons, \q à cause du froment et de l’orge, \q car la moisson des champs est perdue.
fr.R: Agriculteurs, soyez tristes et consternés ! Vous qui cultivez la vigne, criez votre chagrin ! \q Pleurez pour le blé et pour l’orge, \q parce que la récolte des champs est ruinée.

vi.L: Hãy hổ thẹn, hỡi các nông dân; hãy kêu gào, hỡi những người trồng nho, \q vì lúa mì và lúa mạch, \q vì mùa màng ngoài đồng đã mất.
vi.B: Hỡi các nông dân, hãy thất vọng! Hỡi những người trồng nho, hãy kêu gào, \q vì lúa mì và lúa mạch, \q vì mùa màng ngoài đồng đã hư mất.
vi.R: Hỡi các nông dân, hãy buồn rầu thất vọng! Hỡi những người trồng nho, hãy kêu khóc thảm thiết! \q Hãy khóc cho lúa mì và lúa mạch, \q vì mùa màng ngoài đồng đã bị hủy hoại.

sw.L: Aibikeni, enyi wakulima; ombolezeni, enyi watunza mizabibu, \q kwa ajili ya ngano na kwa ajili ya shayiri, \q kwa maana mavuno ya shamba yameangamia.
sw.B: Fadhaikeni, enyi wakulima! Ombolezeni, ninyi mnaotunza mizabibu, \q kwa ajili ya ngano na shayiri, \q kwa sababu mavuno ya shamba yamepotea.
sw.R: Wakulima, huzunikeni na kufadhaika! Ninyi mnaolima zabibu, lieni kwa huzuni! \q Lilieni ngano na shayiri, \q kwa sababu mavuno mashambani yameharibika.

am.L: ገበሬዎች ሆይ፣ እፈሩ፤ የወይን አትክልተኞች ሆይ፣ ዋይ በሉ፤ \q ስለ ስንዴውና ስለ ገብሱ፤ \q የሜዳው መከር ጠፍቷልና።
am.B: እናንተ ገበሬዎች፣ ደንግጡ! የወይን ተክል የምትንከባከቡ፣ ዋይ በሉ፤ \q ስለ ስንዴውና ስለ ገብሱ፤ \q የእርሻው መከር ጠፍቷልና።
am.R: ገበሬዎች ሆይ፣ እዘኑ፤ ደንግጡም! ወይን የምታለሙ ሆይ፣ በሐዘን ጩኹ! \q ስለ ስንዴውና ስለ ገብሱ አልቅሱ፤ \q በእርሻዎቹ ያለው መከር ጠፍቷልና።

hi.L: हे किसानो, लज्जित हो; हे दाख की बारी के मालियो, हाय-हाय करो, \q गेहूँ और जौ के कारण, \q क्योंकि खेत की फ़सल नष्ट हो गई है।
hi.B: हे किसानो, निराश हो जाओ! हे दाख की बारियों की देखभाल करनेवालो, विलाप करो, \q गेहूँ और जौ के लिए, \q क्योंकि खेत की फ़सल नष्ट हो गई है।
hi.R: हे किसानो, दुखी और निराश हो जाओ! हे अंगूर उगानेवालो, दुख से चिल्लाओ! \q गेहूँ और जौ के लिए रोओ, \q क्योंकि खेतों की फ़सल बरबाद हो गई है।

ru.L: Стыдитесь, земледельцы, рыдайте, виноградари, \q о пшенице и о ячмене, \q потому что погиб урожай поля.
ru.B: Придите в смятение, земледельцы! Рыдайте, виноградари, \q о пшенице и ячмене, \q потому что пропал урожай на полях.
ru.R: Земледельцы, горюйте и стыдитесь! Виноградари, кричите от горя! \q Плачьте о пшенице и ячмене, \q потому что урожай на полях погиб.

uk.L: Засоромтеся, хлібороби; ридайте, виноградарі, \q за пшеницею і за ячменем, \q бо загинув урожай поля.
uk.B: Збентежтеся, хлібороби! Ридайте, ви, що доглядаєте лози, \q за пшеницею та ячменем, \q бо врожай поля пропав.
uk.R: Хлібороби, сумуйте й журіться! Ви, що вирощуєте виноград, голосіть з горя! \q Плачте за пшеницею та ячменем, \q бо врожай на полях загинув.

decisions.choice: be ashamed: be dismayed and disappointed, as when hope comes to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for shame. It is used of those whose hopes are disappointed (Jeremiah 14:3-4, of farmers in a drought). It sounds almost the same as the verb "dried up" in verses 10, 12 and 17, and the prophet plays on the two: the crops dry up and the farmers are put to shame.

decisions.choice: wheat and barley: the grain harvest
decisions.reason: Barley ripened first, in spring, and wheat some weeks later. Both are lost, so there is nothing to harvest at all.

decisions.choice: Be dismayed (B); be sad and dismayed (R); you who tend the vines (B); You who grow grapes (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "dismayed", the sense of "ashamed" here (m1), and describe the vinedressers' work.

decisions.choice: Envergonhem-se (L); Fiquem consternados (B); fiquem tristes e desanimados (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the verb of shame; Balanced and Readable say the sense here, hope come to nothing (m1). The sound play with "dried up" (verses 10, 12, 17) cannot be kept in Portuguese and is left to the meaning note.

decisions.choice: लज्जित हो (L); निराश हो जाओ (B); दुखी और निराश हो जाओ (R)
decisions.reason: "Be ashamed" here means to be dismayed when hope comes to nothing (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say that sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Придите в смятение (B); горюйте и стыдитесь (R)
decisions.reason: Be ashamed here means dismay when hope comes to nothing (meaning decision); Literal keeps the verb.

source.text: הַגֶּ֣פֶן הוֹבִ֔ישָׁה וְהַתְּאֵנָ֖ה אֻמְלָ֑לָה רִמּ֞וֹן גַּם־תָּמָ֣ר וְתַפּ֗וּחַ כָּל־עֲצֵ֤י הַשָּׂדֶה֙ יָבֵ֔שׁוּ כִּֽי־הֹבִ֥ישׁ שָׂשׂ֖וֹן מִן־בְּנֵ֥י אָדָֽם׃ס

records.literal_gloss: The vine has dried up, and the fig tree withers; pomegranate, also palm, and apple tree, all [the] trees of the field have dried up; for has dried up joy from [the] children of mankind.

en.L: The vine has dried up, \q and the fig tree withers; \q pomegranate, palm also, and apple tree, all the trees of the field have dried up; \q indeed, joy has dried up from the children of mankind.
en.B: The vine has withered, \q the fig tree droops; \q pomegranate, palm, and apple tree, all the trees of the field are dried up. \q Surely joy has withered away from the people.
en.R: The grapevines are dry, \q and the fig trees are dying. \q The pomegranate trees, palm trees, apple trees, and all the trees in the fields have dried up. \q And the people have lost all their joy.

pt.L: A videira secou, \q e a figueira definha; \q romãzeira, também palmeira, e macieira, todas as árvores do campo secaram; \q sim, a alegria secou dentre os filhos da humanidade.
pt.B: A videira murchou, \q a figueira desfalece; \q a romãzeira, a palmeira e a macieira, todas as árvores do campo estão secas. \q De fato, a alegria murchou e se afastou do povo.
pt.R: As parreiras estão secas, \q e as figueiras estão morrendo. \q As romãzeiras, as palmeiras, as macieiras e todas as árvores dos campos secaram. \q E o povo perdeu toda a sua alegria.

es.L: La vid se ha secado, \q y la higuera se marchita; \q el granado, también la palmera y el manzano, todos los árboles del campo se han secado; \q ciertamente se ha secado la alegría de los hijos de los hombres.
es.B: La vid se ha marchitado, \q la higuera languidece; \q el granado, la palmera y el manzano, todos los árboles del campo están secos. \q Sin duda la alegría se ha marchitado en la gente.
es.R: Las viñas están secas, \q y las higueras se están muriendo. \q Los granados, las palmeras, los manzanos y todos los árboles de los campos se han secado. \q Y la gente ha perdido toda su alegría.

ko.L: 포도나무가 마르고, \q 무화과나무가 시들었다. \q 석류나무도 종려나무도 사과나무도, 들의 모든 나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 참으로 사람의 자식들에게서 기쁨이 말라 버렸다.
ko.B: 포도나무가 마르고 \q 무화과나무가 시들었다. \q 석류나무와 종려나무와 사과나무와 들의 모든 나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 사람들에게서 기쁨이 말라 버린 것이 분명하다.
ko.R: 포도나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 무화과나무도 죽어 간다. \q 석류나무와 종려나무와 사과나무와 들판의 모든 나무가 말라 버렸다. \q 사람들은 기쁨을 다 잃어버렸다.

fr.L: La vigne est desséchée, \q et le figuier dépérit ; \q le grenadier, le palmier aussi, et le pommier, tous les arbres des champs sont desséchés ; \q oui, la joie s’est desséchée loin des fils de l’humanité.
fr.B: La vigne s’est flétrie, \q le figuier languit ; \q le grenadier, le palmier et le pommier, tous les arbres des champs sont desséchés. \q Oui, la joie s’est flétrie chez les gens.
fr.R: Les vignes sont sèches, \q et les figuiers meurent. \q Les grenadiers, les palmiers, les pommiers et tous les arbres des champs sont desséchés. \q Et les gens ont perdu toute leur joie.

vi.L: Cây nho đã khô héo, \q và cây vả tàn úa; \q cây lựu, cả cây chà là, và cây táo, mọi cây ngoài đồng đều đã khô héo; \q thật vậy, niềm vui đã khô héo khỏi con cái loài người.
vi.B: Cây nho đã khô héo, \q cây vả rũ tàn; \q cây lựu, cây chà là và cây táo, mọi cây ngoài đồng đều khô héo. \q Thật vậy, niềm vui đã tàn lụi khỏi loài người.
vi.R: Cây nho khô héo, \q cây vả sắp chết. \q Cây lựu, cây chà là, cây táo và mọi cây ngoài đồng đều đã khô héo. \q Người ta đã mất hết niềm vui.

sw.L: Mzabibu umekauka, \q na mtini unanyauka; \q mkomamanga, mtende pia, na mtofaa, miti yote ya shamba imekauka; \q naam, furaha imekauka kutoka kwa wanadamu.
sw.B: Mzabibu umenyauka, \q mtini umesinyaa; \q mkomamanga, mtende na mtofaa, miti yote ya shamba imekauka. \q Hakika furaha imetoweka kwa watu.
sw.R: Mizabibu imekauka, \q na mitini inakufa. \q Mikomamanga, mitende, mitofaa, na miti yote mashambani imekauka. \q Na watu wamepoteza furaha yao yote.

am.L: ወይኑ ደርቋል፤ \q በለሱም ጠውልጓል፤ \q ሮማኑ፣ ዘንባባውም ደግሞ፣ የፖም ዛፉም፣ የሜዳው ዛፎች ሁሉ ደርቀዋል፤ \q በእርግጥ ደስታ ከሰው ልጆች ደርቋል።
am.B: ወይኑ ደርቋል፤ \q በለሱም ጠውልጓል፤ \q ሮማኑ፣ ዘንባባውና የፖም ዛፉ፣ የሜዳ ዛፎች ሁሉ ደርቀዋል። \q በእርግጥም ደስታ ከሕዝቡ መካከል ጠፍቷል።
am.R: የወይን ተክሎቹ ደርቀዋል፤ \q በለሶቹም እየሞቱ ናቸው። \q ሮማኑ፣ ዘንባባው፣ የፖም ዛፉና በእርሻ ያሉ ዛፎች ሁሉ ደርቀዋል። \q ሕዝቡም ደስታውን ሁሉ አጥቷል።

hi.L: दाखलता सूख गई है, \q और अंजीर का पेड़ मुरझा गया है; \q अनार, खजूर भी, और सेब का पेड़, मैदान के सब पेड़ सूख गए हैं; \q सचमुच, मनुष्य की सन्तान में से आनंद सूख गया है।
hi.B: दाखलता मुरझा गई है, \q अंजीर का पेड़ कुम्हला गया है; \q अनार, खजूर और सेब के पेड़, मैदान के सब पेड़ सूख गए हैं। \q सचमुच लोगों में से आनंद मिट गया है।
hi.R: अंगूर की बेलें सूख गई हैं, \q और अंजीर के पेड़ मर रहे हैं। \q अनार, खजूर, सेब और खेतों के सब पेड़ सूख गए हैं। \q और लोगों का सारा आनंद जाता रहा है।

ru.L: Лоза засохла, \q и смоковница вянет; \q гранатовое дерево, и пальма, и яблоня, все деревья поля засохли; \q поистине, иссякла радость у сынов человеческих.
ru.B: Виноградная лоза засохла, \q смоковница поникла; \q гранатовое дерево, пальма и яблоня — все деревья в поле засохли. \q Поистине, радость иссякла у людей.
ru.R: Виноградные лозы засохли, \q и смоковницы погибают. \q Гранатовые деревья, пальмы, яблони и все деревья в полях засохли. \q И люди потеряли всякую радость.

uk.L: Лоза висохла, \q і смоковниця вʼяне; \q гранат, і пальма також, і яблуня, усі дерева поля висохли; \q так, висохла радість у синів людських.
uk.B: Лоза зівʼяла, \q смоковниця никне; \q гранат, пальма і яблуня, усі дерева поля всохли. \q Справді, радість зівʼяла в людей.
uk.R: Виноградні лози сухі, \q а інжирні дерева гинуть. \q Гранатові дерева, пальми, яблуні й усі дерева в полях всохли. \q І люди втратили всю свою радість.

decisions.choice: joy has dried up: the same verb as for the vine, with a play on "be ashamed"
decisions.reason: The verb used for the vine at the start of the verse is used again for joy at the end: the joy of the people withers with their trees. The same verb can be heard as "be put to shame" (see verse 11). Harvest was a time of great joy (Isaiah 9:2; 16:10), and now there is none.

decisions.choice: apple tree: perhaps another fruit tree, such as the apricot or quince
decisions.reason: The tree is named with the word for apple in later Hebrew, but it is not certain which fruit tree is meant in Bible times (Song of Songs 2:3; Proverbs 25:11).

decisions.choice: the children of mankind (L); the people (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, which means human beings. Balanced and Readable say "the people".

decisions.choice: os filhos da humanidade (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase for human beings with a word that includes everyone; the English has no gender span here, so neither does the Portuguese. The verb "secar" is used for the vine and for joy at Literal, keeping the repetition of m1.

decisions.choice: "furaha imekauka" (joy has dried up)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one verb for the trees and for joy, as the Hebrew does (m1); Balanced and Readable say joy has vanished. "Mtofaa" (apple tree) is formed from "tofaa" (Proverbs 25:11).

decisions.choice: "ደርቋል" for both the vine and joy (L)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses one verb for the vine that dries up and the joy that dries up; Literal keeps one Amharic verb for both, so the picture stays.

decisions.choice: у сынов человеческих
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "sons of man"; the English has no gender span here, and the phrase means all people.

source.text: חִגְר֨וּ וְסִפְד֜וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֗ים הֵילִ֨ילוּ֙ מְשָׁרְתֵ֣י מִזְבֵּ֔חַ בֹּ֚אוּ לִ֣ינוּ בַשַּׂקִּ֔ים מְשָׁרְתֵ֖י אֱלֹהָ֑י כִּ֥י נִמְנַ֛ע מִבֵּ֥ית אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֖ם מִנְחָ֥ה וָנָֽסֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Gird yourselves and lament, the priests; wail, ministers of [the] altar; come, spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God; for withheld from [the] house of your God [are] grain offering and drink offering.

en.L: Put on [sackcloth] and lament, you priests; \q wail, ministers of the altar; \q come, spend the night in sackcloth, ministers of my God! \q For grain offering and drink offering are withheld from the house of your God.
en.B: Put on sackcloth and mourn, you priests! \q Wail, you who serve at the altar! \q Come, spend the night in sackcloth, you who serve my God! \q For grain offerings and drink offerings are kept back from the house of your God.
en.R: Priests, put on sackcloth and mourn! \q You who serve at the altar, cry out in grief! \q You who serve my God, come and spend the night dressed in sackcloth. \q There is no grain or wine to offer in the temple of your God.

pt.L: Cinjam-se [de pano de saco] e pranteiem, sacerdotes; \q lamentem, ministros do altar; \q venham, passem a noite em pano de saco, ministros do meu Deus! \q Porque a oferta de cereal e a oferta de bebida foram retidas da casa do Deus de vocês.
pt.B: Vistam pano de saco e chorem de luto, sacerdotes! \q Gritem de dor, vocês que servem no altar! \q Venham, passem a noite vestidos de pano de saco, vocês que servem o meu Deus! \q Pois as ofertas de cereal e as ofertas de bebida deixaram de chegar à casa do Deus de vocês.
pt.R: Sacerdotes, vistam pano de saco e chorem de luto! \q Vocês que servem no altar, gritem de tristeza! \q Vocês que servem o meu Deus, venham passar a noite vestidos de pano de saco. \q Não há cereal nem vinho para oferecer no templo do Deus de vocês.

es.L: {{plural_you:Cíñanse|Ceñíos}} [de cilicio] y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} lamento, sacerdotes; \q {{plural_you:giman|gemid}}, ministros del altar; \q {{plural_you:vengan|venid}}, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche en cilicio, ministros de mi Dios, \q porque la ofrenda de cereal y la libación han sido retenidas de la casa de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Vístanse|Vestíos}} de cilicio y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo, sacerdotes! \q ¡{{plural_you:Giman|Gemid}}, los que sirven en el altar! \q ¡{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}}, {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche vestidos de cilicio, los que sirven a mi Dios! \q Porque las ofrendas de cereal y las libaciones faltan en la casa de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.
es.R: Sacerdotes, ¡{{plural_you:vístanse|vestíos}} con ropa áspera de luto y {{plural_you:hagan|haced}} duelo! \q Los que sirven en el altar, ¡{{plural_you:lloren|llorad}} de dolor! \q Los que sirven a mi Dios, {{plural_you:vengan|venid}} y {{plural_you:pasen|pasad}} la noche vestidos con ropa áspera de luto. \q Ya no hay grano ni vino para ofrecer en el templo de {{plural_you:su Dios|vuestro Dios}}.

ko.L: 제사장들아, [굵은 베옷을] 두르고 애곡하여라. \q 제단을 섬기는 자들아, 통곡하여라. \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 자들아, 와서 굵은 베옷을 입고 밤을 지새워라. \q 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물이 너희 하나님의 집에 들어오지 못하게 되었다.
ko.B: 제사장들아, 굵은 베옷을 입고 슬피 울어라! \q 제단을 섬기는 자들아, 통곡하여라! \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 자들아, 와서 굵은 베옷을 입은 채 밤을 지새워라! \q 곡식 제물과 부어 드리는 제물을 너희 하나님의 집에 드릴 수 없게 되었다.
ko.R: 제사장들아, 굵은 베옷을 입고 슬퍼하여라! \q 제단에서 섬기는 사람들아, 슬피 울부짖어라! \q 내 하나님을 섬기는 사람들아, 와서 굵은 베옷을 입은 채로 밤을 새워라. \q 너희 하나님의 성전에 바칠 곡식도 포도주도 없다.

fr.L: Ceignez-[vous du sac] et lamentez-vous, prêtres ; \q gémissez, serviteurs de l’autel ; \q venez, passez la nuit vêtus de sacs, serviteurs de mon Dieu ! \q Car l’offrande végétale et la libation sont refusées à la maison de votre Dieu.
fr.B: Mettez le sac et pleurez, prêtres ! \q Gémissez, vous qui servez à l’autel ! \q Venez, passez la nuit vêtus de sacs, vous qui servez mon Dieu ! \q Car les offrandes végétales et les libations manquent à la maison de votre Dieu.
fr.R: Prêtres, mettez des sacs de deuil et pleurez ! \q Vous qui servez à l’autel, criez votre chagrin ! \q Vous qui servez mon Dieu, venez passer la nuit habillés de sacs de deuil. \q Il n’y a plus de grain ni de vin à offrir dans le temple de votre Dieu.

vi.L: Hãy thắt [vải thô] và than khóc, hỡi các thầy tế lễ; \q hãy kêu gào, hỡi những người phục vụ bàn thờ; \q hãy đến, mặc vải thô mà thức suốt đêm, hỡi những người phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi! \q Vì tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán đã bị cầm lại khỏi nhà Đức Chúa Trời của các người.
vi.B: Hỡi các thầy tế lễ, hãy mặc vải thô và than khóc! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ bàn thờ, hãy kêu gào! \q Hỡi những người phục vụ Đức Chúa Trời của tôi, hãy đến, mặc vải thô mà thức suốt đêm! \q Vì tế lễ ngũ cốc và lễ quán không còn được dâng trong nhà Đức Chúa Trời của các người.
